behavioral_notes.observation: The model is not a real table: init() drops and recreates a Postgres VIEW. The view UNION ALLs two row sources and aggregates them per employee/day: (1) attendance rows from hr_attendance (worked_hours -> attendance, id negated to avoid PK collision, check_in date-truncated in the employee's resource_calendar timezone) and (2) timesheet rows from account_analytic_line where project_id IS NOT NULL (unit_amount -> timesheet). The outer query GROUPs BY employee_id, date, company_id, emp_cost and sums each side, so one row reconciles hours-present vs hours-timesheeted for a given employee on a given day. No ORM table exists; all values are computed in SQL.

total_attendance = coalesce(sum(attendance),0); total_timesheet = coalesce(sum(timesheet),0); total_difference = total_attendance - total_timesheet. The difference is the headline KPI (the graph view plots only total_difference): it flags how much of an employee's recorded presence is NOT covered by logged timesheets (positive) or over-logged (negative). All three are Float hours, rendered with the timesheet_uom widget in the pivot/graph views.

Each hours sum is multiplied by hr_employee.hourly_cost (emp_cost, carried through the subquery and the GROUP BY) to value the reconciliation in money: timesheets_cost = sum(timesheet)*emp_cost, attendance_cost = sum(attendance)*emp_cost, cost_difference = (attendance-timesheet)*emp_cost. NULLIF(...,0) blanks zero results so empty cells are hidden. This converts the hours gap into a labour-cost variance per employee/day.

formatted_read_group is overridden so that when no explicit order is passed but a groupby exists, date groupings default to DESC (most recent first) while other groupby specs keep their natural order. This only affects pivot/graph sort presentation, not the underlying reconciliation data.

The module patches ir.ui.menu to hide the 'Timesheets / Attendance Analysis' report menu from any user who lacks hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_user, by appending the menu id to the blacklist. Visibility of the analytics is thus gated on the timesheet-user group, on top of the four ir.rule record rules (multi-company scope, own-employee for users, all-rows for approvers and timesheet managers).

No JS/OWL assets ship with this module: extract_frontend reports 0 js files, 0 xml templates, no OWL components, registry adds, patches or asset bundles. The UI is purely declarative XML (search + pivot + graph views reusing the inherited timesheet_uom field widget); all reconciliation logic lives in the SQL view.

view tz lookup: resource_calendar via hr_version.resource_calendar_id
information_flows: read-flow: SQL view aggregates hr_attendance + account_analytic_line per employee/day (no writes back)
side-effect: ir.ui.menu._load_menus_blacklist hides report menu for non hr_timesheet users
consumes: hr_employee.hourly_cost to value hours into labour cost
consumes: resource_calendar.tz to date-bucket attendance in employee local time

capabilities: Reconcile Recorded Attendance against Logged Timesheets
Compute Time Difference (presence vs timesheeted hours) per Employee/Day
Value the Time Gap as Labour-Cost Variance
Analyze Timesheet/Attendance Variance (pivot & graph) by Employee, Department, Team and Period
value_streams: Time-reconciliation reporting: record attendance + log timesheets -> SQL view unions and aggregates per employee/day -> surface hours and cost difference in pivot/graph for review
policies: 4 record rules: multi-company scope; user sees only own employee; approver and timesheet-manager see all rows
ir.ui.menu blacklist hides the analysis menu from users without hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_user
timesheet source restricted to lines with project_id set; both sides limited to dates <= CURRENT_DATE
metrics: total_difference (hours gap, headline KPI on graph)

classification.rationale: hr_timesheet_attendance is a read-only HR analytics bridge with no business object of its own: its single model is an _auto=False SQL view that reconciles attendance (hr_attendance) against timesheets (account_analytic_line). It is a Stabell & Fjeldstad support value configuration (a firm-infrastructure/HR control activity), not a primary chain/shop/network flow, since it produces no delivered output and only measures and values labour-time variance. It maps to APQC PCF 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital -- specifically time & attendance management/analytics -- because it monitors workforce time recording and surfaces the present-vs-logged hours and cost gap for control and payroll/billing assurance.

standard_capabilities: out-of-box SQL-view report unioning attendance worked_hours and project timesheet unit_amount per employee/day
hours difference (presence minus timesheeted) plus matching labour-cost difference using employee hourly_cost
pivot and graph analysis with timesheet UoM, grouped by employee/date with My Team and My Department filters
three-tier visibility (own user / approver / manager) via record rules and menu blacklisting
typical_fits: verifying employees timesheet the hours they were present (compliance / billing assurance)
spotting under- or over-logging per employee or department before payroll or customer invoicing
valuing the attendance/timesheet gap as a cost variance for management review
common_gaps: no drill-down to the underlying attendance or timesheet records (aggregate view, disable_linking)
no approval/exception workflow on detected differences (report only, no actions)
no tolerance thresholds or alerting on excessive gaps
timesheets without a project (project_id NULL) are excluded, so non-project time is invisible

open_questions: Whether downstream apps (payroll, invoicing) read total_difference/cost_difference or it is review-only.
How the resource_calendar timezone lookup behaves for employees with no current_version_id / resource_calendar.
Whether overnight attendances spanning midnight are mis-bucketed by the check_in-date truncation.
